input.quote: Customer acknowledges that the Termination for Convenience Fee and the Termination for Cause Fee are each a reasonable approximation of such damages and shall be deemed to be liquidated damages and not a penalty.
input.rationale: § 13.5 deems two Customer-payable amounts "liquidated damages and not a penalty": the § 11.1 Termination for Convenience Fee and the § 11.2(A) Termination for Cause Fee, each a REDACTED percentage of "Estimated Remaining Value" (months remaining to end of Term x the greater of the Monthly Base Fee or average monthly Fees) and each expressly carved out of the § 13.4 cap, with one of them triggered by Customer's Event of Default. That fails all three fallback elements and sits at or near walk-away, so a redline is warranted. Target level is fallback: op 1 quantifies the single fee at three months' average Fees; op 3 deletes the Termination for Cause Fee and substitutes that same early-termination fee (retiring the defined term, so the dangling § 13.4 carve-out sentence goes with it) while preserving the Expenses reimbursement verbatim; op 4 removes the retired term from § 13.5 and states the exclusivity once. Per the verifier, the duplicated "and no other termination fee, liquidated damages or penalty" tail in § 11.2(A) is removed and exclusivity is enacted only in § 13.5. Op 2 is a conforming repair, not a new term: deleting "Customer or " from the § 11.1 scoping sentence so § 11.1 and revised § 11.2(A) agree that the fee is owed on a Customer-default termination, while § 11.2(B) and § 11.1 continue to impose no fee on an M&I default. Housekeeping confirmed: "Estimated Remaining Value" (Definition N) appears only in p0039, p0187 and p0189, so it is left intact and simply unused; the cap is deliberately anchored to the Effective Date of Termination rather than the definition's "event giving rise to termination rights," which satisfies the three-months-of-fees element. Preferred is not reached because § 13.5 still deems the fee liquidated damages payable by Customer; noted, not pursued. Also noted only: § 9.2(D) Service Level Credits to us are REDACTED, and § 8.13 collection fees/Damages and default repricing are pricing/indemnity mechanics rather than liquidated amounts. Quantum is argued once here, not duplicated under the convenience-termination rule.

mappings.element: Any Customer-payable liquidated amount is only an early-termination fee.
The early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.

proposal.summary: Cap the Termination for Convenience Fee at three months' average Fees, align the § 11.1 scoping sentence with § 11.2(A), substitute that single fee for the Termination for Cause Fee, and state once in § 13.5 that it is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our preferred position is that Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties; as a fallback we accept a single early-termination fee capped at three months' fees. We cap the Termination for Convenience Fee at three months' average Fees, delete the separate Termination for Cause Fee so that same fee is the only charge on any early termination other than an M&I default, and state once in § 13.5 that it is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.

ops.oldText: Customer may terminate this Agreement during the Term upon at least one (1) years' written notice to M&I, provided that Customer pays M&I an early termination fee ("Termination for Convenience Fee") in an amount equal to REDACTED of the Estimated Remaining Value.
ops.newText: Customer may terminate this Agreement during the Term upon at least one (1) years' written notice to M&I, provided that Customer pays M&I an early termination fee ("Termination for Convenience Fee") in an amount equal to three (3) times the average monthly Fees payable by Customer during the three (3) months prior to the Effective Date of Termination.

ops.oldText: other than pursuant to an Event of Default on the part of Customer or M&I
ops.newText: other than pursuant to an Event of Default on the part of M&I

ops.oldText: then Customer shall pay M&I a termination fee ("Termination for Cause Fee") in an amount equal to REDACTED of the Estimated Remaining Value, payable as set forth in Section 11.1 above. In addition to the foregoing, Customer shall pay to M&I, reasonable Expenses in connection with the disposition of equipment, facilities and contracts related to M&I's performance of the Services on behalf of Customer. The Termination for Cause Fee shall not be subject to the limitations set forth in Section 13.4.
ops.newText: then Customer shall pay M&I the Termination for Convenience Fee determined and payable as set forth in Section 11.1 above. In addition to the foregoing, Customer shall pay to M&I, reasonable Expenses in connection with the disposition of equipment, facilities and contracts related to M&I's performance of the Services on behalf of Customer.
